prediction:
#13, the wide-line CAP rule.

WHAT THIS IS.  #13's extent phase landed exact and left ~908 px of
whole-capture coverage residual over the 48 non-void Line_* captures -- 493
ours-only, 98.8% of it within w/2 + 2 px of a vertex.  That class is the CAP,
and line-extent-phase-exact.json explicitly declined to predict it ("WHAT I DO
NOT PREDICT: the cap and join phase").  This file predicts it.  It cites
line-extent-phase-exact.json as the arm-specification it inherits the
tripwires from.

THE RULE, derived from the goldens, no fitted constant.  The E-band and the
perpendicular butt cap are both right; the missing constraint is axis-aligned
on the MINOR axis.  The footprint never reaches past the endpoints' own minor
coordinates extended by w/2 -- the WIDTH, not the widened extent E -- with
both bounds rounded OUTWARD to whole pixel indices:

    minor index i is lit only if  floor(m_min - w/2) <= i <= ceil(m_max + w/2)

on the same 1/16 grid the extent rule already uses.  It bites only at the two
tips of the parallelogram, which is exactly where the residual was: inside the
segment the E-band and the perpendicular slab are both tighter.  Clipping by
those two planes turns the parallelogram into a hexagon, so max_vertices goes
4 -> 6 and 12 -> 18.

The outward rounding is forced by the data, not chosen: at one width and one
|slope| the low side stops 31.5 px past its endpoint and the high side reaches
32.5 (Line_0063.7, LLoop4 vs LLoop0).  A centre-sampled +-w/2 band scores 497
px, WORSE than the 412 px it was meant to fix.

WHAT IS PREDICTED, AND WHY IT IS A BOUND AND NOT A VALUE.

The clip is scored offline by rasterising the polygon emit_line() emits and
XORing it against the golden ink.  That rasterisation takes a TIE BIAS, and
the choice of bias moves the answer by more than the effect being measured:

    tie = 1e-9    before the clip  414 px    after   21 px
    tie = 1/256   before the clip  935 px    after  544 px

1/256 is the bias the DEVICE pushes: vk/draw.c's geom_line_params() sets
lineTieBias = 1/(2^subPixelPrecisionBits * surface_scale_factor), and Adreno
reports 8 bits.  So 21 px is a clean measurement of the geometry alone and is
NOT a device prediction; quoting it as one would be off by 25x.  The offline
model at 1/256 predicts arm A at 935 px against ~908 px measured on a real
device arm by the extent lane -- within 3%, from an independent instrument,
which is why that column is the one trusted here.

The residual above 544 px is the tie bias interacting with the rasteriser's
own vertex quantisation.  It is deliberately NOT chased: the bias is pinned by
the extent legs (1,911 of 41,892 golden band edges land exactly on a pixel
centre, worth 550-580 of the 8,890 fit-set cuts) and by subPixelPrecisionBits.
Trading those away to win coverage pixels would be a bad trade made blind.

LEG C1 -- THE CAP LEG.  Golden-constrained, coverage only, so it reads nothing
from the model and a patch cannot make it true by construction; and because it
compares ink MASKS, #13's separate and much larger overlap-COLOUR residual
cannot move it in either direction.

  docs/testing/line_cap_phase.py --vs-goldens <armB captures>

PREDICTED: at most 600 mismatched px over the 48 non-void Line_* captures.
ARM A: ~908 px (extent fix, no cap clip).
FAILS IF: above 600 px.

WHY 600 IS A DISCRIMINATOR AND NOT A FORMALITY, stated before the arm so it
cannot be read back afterwards.  The bound is set so that it holds under
EITHER modelling of the tie -- 21 px and 544 px both clear it -- while arm A's
own 908 px does not.  So the leg separates "the cap clip is drawn and works"
from "nothing happened", which is the only distinction the offline model is
entitled to make given the tie uncertainty.  A bound is honest here and an
exact value would not be: registering 544 as a value would turn the ordinary
device-vs-model gap into a violated check.

LEG C2 -- NOTHING GETS WORSE.  ab_compare per capture over Line_width and
Blend_tests: 0 captures classed worse.  Blend_tests is on the disc because the
geometry push-constant range is declared on EVERY graphics pipeline, whether
or not it has a geometry shader (two layouts are compatible for a descriptor
set only if their push-constant ranges match), so a mistake there shows up on
a suite that draws no wide lines at all.  That is the point of including it.
FAILS IF: any capture in either suite is classed worse.

LEG C3 -- THE TRIPWIRES, inherited from line-extent-phase-exact.json, must not
move at all:
  Line_width/Fill_0000.0, Fill_0001.0, Fill_0032.0 -- fill mode; a line change
    must not touch them
  Line_width/Line_0000.0 -- the suite's only pixel-exact capture; a zero-width
    line covers no pixel centre and the draw is dropped
  Line_width/Line_0064.0 .. Line_0064.7, Line_FFFFFFFF -- VOID: the width
    register holds nine bits of eighths, 64.0 does not fit, hardware drew all
    nine at 1.0, and their golden ink masks are byte-identical to
    Line_0001.0's.  A fix that draws them at 64 makes them worse.
FAILS IF: any of these moves at all.

WHAT I DO NOT PREDICT.  The COLOUR at an overlap -- #13's separate priority
rule and 76.3% of the issue's residual; this is a coverage measurement.  The
~544 px tie-bias residual, for the reason above.  The GL renderer, which is
lane.remote's territory and untouched here.  Any total for Point size, Point
params, Swath width, Smoothing control, Stipple tests or 2D Lines.

A CAVEAT ON THE OFFLINE MODEL.  It rasterises with exact-float half-plane
tests at exact pixel centres; the real rasteriser quantises vertices to the
1/256 grid first and then applies its own fill rule.  The truth lies between
the two tie columns above, which is precisely why C1 is a bound spanning
both and not a point estimate at either end.

cites.note: the extent phase this builds on; its 'WHAT I DO NOT PREDICT' names the cap as unpredicted, and LEG C3's tripwires are its must_not_move list carried forward unchanged.
